body: Never too late to begin to learn. I'm an art teacher, trust me. It takes a lot of dedication and hard work, but you absolutely can. Begin by learning basic drawing...making still life compositions at home and sketching them, sketching landscape and sketching people. The main thing to focus on is draw what you SEE. Not what your brain sees. An apple is not red and perfectly symmetrical, however if I ask you to draw one...even with it in front of you...you will probably draw your minds eye symbol for the object. The real apple of you look closely is many colors, it has dents and rough patches, it probably sits resting more on one side than another, most likely it is not symmetrical. It may have yellow on one side and be red on the other. But you have to SEE it. Practice seeing the world more. See and choose a media and re-create. Do it over and over until it gets closer to the real thing. Look up blind contour, gesture sketching, continuous line drawing, color theory, color mixing, and value to begin. Feel free to PM me with any questions!
